sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the north-western riverfront of National Park, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. The Delaware River fills the left side of the sheet, and a long row of summer cottages stands on narrow lots along the top of the river bank, many of them carrying painted names such as Riverview, Silver Star, Oldreserve Cottage, Silverun, Winfield, Hunter, Marion Ho., Aberdeen, Clark, Idle Hours, Old Homestead, Algonquin, Week End and Sunset. Behind them the large lot 124 is mostly open ground, edged by the dashed top of the bluff, with a few dwellings on its inland side. 2nd Street runs along the right edge of the sheet, drawn on its western side only, crossed by Mercer Street and Monmouth Street near the top, New Jersey Avenue, the 100 foot wide Columbia Avenue and Monument Avenue at the bottom. Grand View Avenue curves from New Jersey Avenue down to Columbia Avenue, and Minden Place, a short lane with cottages named Mattson and Restawile, leads off it towards the Road to Boat Landing, which runs from Columbia Avenue to the river along the foot of the sheet. Between New Jersey and Columbia Avenues stands the National Park Hotel, open in summer only, with a pavilion beside it on 2nd Street. Blocks 124, 125 and 129 are numbered; block 129 holds dwellings and stores facing Monument Avenue. Water pipes and fire hydrants are marked along the streets. Sheet 3 adjoins on the right and sheet 7 at the bottom left.
notes: Columbia Avenue east of the Grand View Avenue junction is today's Columbia Boulevard; its western end, curving down to Monument Avenue, is today's North Grand Avenue.
Grand View Avenue does not follow a modern street: today's North Grand Avenue runs straighter, to the east of its curve.
Minden Place is roughly today's Central Avenue; the Road to Boat Landing is roughly today's Beach Hill Road.
National Park Hotel (open summer only) and pavilion on 2nd Street between New Jersey and Columbia Avenues.

50 ft. North-western riverfront: river-bank cottages, 2nd St (west side only), New Jersey Av, Columbia Av, Grand View Av, Minden Pl, Road to Boat Landing, Monument Av; National Park Hotel. One part, turned (north upper left, rotation about -47). Few modern junctions survive: placed from four hand-picked points on 2nd St and Monument Av.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the central blocks of the borough of National Park, in the part of town laid out on a grid running north-west to south-east, square to the Delaware River front. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. Pennsylvania Avenue, New Jersey Avenue, Columbia Avenue and Monument Avenue cross the sheet from side to side, with Delaware Avenue along the top; 2nd Street runs down the left edge, 3rd Street down the middle and 4th Street along the right edge. The blocks are numbered 118 to 131 and are divided into deep lots numbered in small series along each street. Most lots are empty; the buildings drawn are scattered frame dwellings with outbuildings, an auto storage and repair building and a hotel in the lower blocks near Columbia Avenue and Monument Avenue, and a few small commercial buildings. Water pipes of 4 inches and 6 inches are shown in the avenues and a few hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked. The vertical line of the borough limits is drawn along the left side of 3rd Street in the upper blocks, and the angled street grid beyond it in the upper left corner, outside the borough and drawn in outline, is not part of the area georeferenced here. The scale bar and the sheet number are at the foot of the sheet. Adjoining sheets are numbered 2 on the left, 4 on the right and 8 at the foot.
notes: Columbia Avenue on this sheet is the street now called Columbia Boulevard.
The angled blocks at the upper left (Mercer, Monmouth and a second 3rd Street) lie outside the borough limits and are left out of the mask of this part.
50 ft. Delaware, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Columbia (today Columbia Blvd), Monument Avs; 2nd, 3rd, 4th Sts. One part; mask notched at upper left (outline grid of Mercer/Monmouth outside the borough).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the northern edge of the borough of National Park, where the square street grid of the central blocks meets the angled streets near the borough limits. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. In the left half, Delaware Avenue, Pennsylvania Avenue, New Jersey Avenue, Columbia Avenue and Monument Avenue cross the sheet, with 4th Street at the left edge and 5th Street running down the middle; below Columbia Avenue 5th Street is lettered Columbia Boulevard and curves to the south-east. The blocks are numbered 120, 123, 128 and 132 and are divided into deep lots with scattered frame dwellings, a few stores and outbuildings. On the right, past the dashed line of the borough limits, the streets turn to follow a different bearing: Pennsylvania Avenue and New Jersey Avenue continue at a slant and East Columbia Boulevard and Wesley Avenue run diagonally across the lower right, with long narrow blocks numbered 190, 190 1/2, 191 and 140 and small frame dwellings and a greenhouse. A strip across the top, above Delaware Avenue, shows the borough limits line and the ends of Lafayette Avenue, Fifth Street and Sixth Street, drawn in outline. Water pipes of 4 inches and 6 inches are marked along the avenues, with hydrants. The scale bar and a compass rose are at the foot. Adjoining sheets are 3 on the left, 5 on the right and 9 at the foot.
notes: Columbia Avenue on this sheet is the street now called Columbia Boulevard; the street lettered Columbia Boulevard south of it is the present North 5th Street.
5th Street between Delaware Avenue and Columbia Avenue is North 5th Street today.
The street lettered ...ood St. in the strip at the top could not be read with confidence and is left out of the street names.
The line lettered Borough Limits runs across the top and diagonally down the right side of the sheet.

50 ft. Delaware, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Columbia Avs, E. Columbia Blvd, Wesley, Monument Avs; 4th St, 5th St, Columbia Blvd (today North 5th St); Lafayette Av, Fifth St, Wood St, Sixth St outlined at the top. Left half square grid; the angled right half beyond the borough limits has no control and follows the left half.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the eastern edge of the borough of National Park, where the square grid of the town meets the angled streets along the borough limits and the Red Bank side. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. In the upper left, Pennsylvania Avenue and New Jersey Avenue run from the left edge toward Grove Avenue, with blocks numbered 190 and 191 holding a few frame dwellings and sheds. In the upper right, outside the borough and drawn in outline under the note No Exposure, long narrow blocks numbered 192, 193 and 193 1/2 lie between 8th Street, 9th Street and 10th Street, with Pennsylvania Avenue running diagonally through them. East Columbia Boulevard crosses the middle of the sheet, and below it Wesley Avenue, Asbury Avenue and Cookman Avenue run toward St. John's Walk, with blocks numbered 141, 149, 144, 153 and 146 of small dwellings, an auto repair shop and a pavilion. A large open tract at the right is marked Camp Meeting Ground. Water pipes of 4 inches and 6 inches run in the avenues, with hydrants. The scale bar is at the foot. Adjoining sheets are 4 on the left, 6 on the right, 9 at lower left, 10 below and 11 at lower right.
notes: The Camp Meeting Ground at the right edge is drawn as an open tract with a pavilion.
Saint John's Walk is St. John's Walk as printed; today's Saint Johns Walk follows it.
50 ft. Pennsylvania, New Jersey Avs, E. Columbia Blvd, Wesley, Asbury, Cookman Avs, Grove Av, St. John's Walk, 8th to 10th Sts; Camp Meeting Ground. One part, rotation about -29.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the south-eastern blocks of the borough of National Park around Philadelphia Avenue and East Columbia Boulevard. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. Chestnut Avenue, Philadelphia Avenue, East Columbia Boulevard, Wesley Avenue and Asbury Avenue run across the sheet from left to right, crossed by St. James Walk near the left edge, Oak Avenue in the middle and Lincoln Avenue at the right edge. The regular blocks, numbered 94, 154, 147, 142, 143, 148, 195 and 196, are divided into narrow lots and hold rows of frame dwellings with small outbuildings, a few of them marked with automobile garages. Maple Avenue runs diagonally through the upper right corner, with angled blocks 197 and 198 beside it, and the upper left holds angled blocks 193 and 193 1/2 between 9th Street and 10th Street, drawn in outline near the borough limits, which are marked by a dashed line across the upper part of the sheet. Water pipes of 6 inches are marked in Chestnut Avenue and along Maple Avenue, with hydrants at several corners. A compass rose is at the top and the scale bar is at the foot.
notes: The street at the right edge, lettered Lincoln Av., is North Lincoln Avenue today.
The angled blocks at the upper left lie outside the borough limits and are drawn in outline.
50 ft. Chestnut, Philadelphia Avs, E. Columbia Blvd, Wesley, Asbury, Oak, Lincoln, Maple Avs, St. James Walk, 9th, 10th Sts, Manduit. One part, rotation about -22.

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 7 covers the river settlement of Eagleton, north of National Park, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet's north arrow points straight up, but the fitted placement puts north about 20 degrees to the left of the top of the page. Red Bank or Belmont Avenue runs down the right half of the part to the Delaware River, which bends around the upper right corner; Division runs parallel to it at the right edge. Across the lower part run Front, marked as not open, then Reeves and 2nd Street at the bottom, crossed by Donop and Howard. Most of the area between Front and the heavy dividing line is the open lot 40 and Red Bank Park, a summer playground whose buildings are used in summer only; the park holds a first aid house and a dwelling. Blocks 41 to 51 are numbered; the built blocks are along Red Bank or Belmont Avenue, where small dwellings and auto garages stand, together with a store, and along River Place, a short arbitrary-named lane of dwellings on the river side of block 46. Blocks 42, 44, 47, 48 and 49 along Reeves and 2nd Street are laid out in lots with only a few dwellings and a stable. The scale bar is printed in Red Bank Park. The upper left of the sheet, beyond the heavy line, is part 2 (the riverfront of National Park, drawn at another angle).
notes: Printed as 'Red Bank or Belmont Av.'; today Red Bank Avenue.
Donop south of Reeves and Reeves itself are today one street, Front Street, which turns from 2nd Street to Red Bank Avenue; the drawn Front is not a modern street.
The north arrow is drawn pointing up, but the street grid fits about 20 degrees off it.

50 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 Eagleton (Red Bank or Belmont Av, Front (not open), Reeves, 2nd St, Donop, Howard, Division, River Pl, Red Bank Park; drawn north arrow up but the grid fits about +20 degrees); part 2 upper left, the riverfront of National Park at Monument Av, 2nd St, Columbia Av (today North Grand Av), Standish Pl, Road to Boat Landing (rotation about -47).

sheet-7-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 7 is the upper left of the sheet, above a heavy dividing line: the south-western end of National Park's riverfront along the Delaware River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, at a different angle from part 1 below it. Monument Avenue crosses the top right from 2nd Street, at the right edge, to Columbia Avenue, which curves down the middle of the part; the Road to Boat Landing runs along the top from Columbia Avenue to the river. West of Columbia Avenue, Standish Place, an arbitrary-named lane, runs parallel to the river between two rows of lots, and a long row of small dwellings, many marked as summer cottages, lines the river bank. Lot 189 holds most of these houses, including one named Polly Anna, and a few bath houses stand at the top near the boat landing. East of Columbia Avenue, block 133 faces Monument Avenue with dwellings on numbered lots in the 1000s; the rest of the part, towards the dividing line, is open ground marked no exposure. Water pipes run along Monument Avenue and Standish Place. Sheet 2 adjoins at the top.
notes: Columbia Avenue here is today's North Grand Avenue; Standish Place is roughly today's Bluff Road and the Road to Boat Landing roughly today's Beach Hill Road.
The riverfront lots have been rebuilt since; only the junctions on Monument Avenue and the head of the Road to Boat Landing could be matched to modern streets.

50 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 Eagleton (Red Bank or Belmont Av, Front (not open), Reeves, 2nd St, Donop, Howard, Division, River Pl, Red Bank Park; drawn north arrow up but the grid fits about +20 degrees); part 2 upper left, the riverfront of National Park at Monument Av, 2nd St, Columbia Av (today North Grand Av), Standish Pl, Road to Boat Landing (rotation about -47).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the north-western corner of the borough of National Park, on the grid that runs north-west to south-east, square to the Delaware River front. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left, as the compass rose at upper right shows. Monument Avenue crosses the top of the sheet on a diagonal from upper left to right, with a 50 foot width marked at several points; below it a grid of streets runs down the page: Wesley Avenue, Asbury Avenue and Simpson Avenue cross 2nd Street at the left edge, 3rd Street in the middle and 4th Street at the right edge, where only one side of the street is drawn. The blocks are numbered 134, 135, 137, 138, 149, 150, 157 and 158 and are divided into long narrow lots numbered in the 500s and 1000s. Most lots are empty or hold a single frame dwelling of one to two and a half storeys with a small auto garage or shed. The notable buildings are St. Matthew's R.C. Church on the triangular block between Monument Avenue and Wesley Avenue, heated by furnace and lit by electricity, and a Boy Scouts building on Monument Avenue. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along 2nd Street, Wesley, Asbury and Simpson Avenues, with fire hydrants at several corners. A diagonal line down the left edge marks the western limit of the area drawn, with block 133 outside it. Sheet 3 adjoins at the top, sheet 9 at the right and sheet 12 at the bottom. The scale bar is at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Modern names, from OpenStreetMap: 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets are North 2nd Street, North 3rd Street and North 4th Street.
St. Matthew's R.C. Church on Monument Avenue between 3rd and 4th Streets.
2nd Street is drawn at the left edge with only its eastern side; its junctions were not used for control.
50 ft. Monument, Wesley, Asbury, Simpson Avs; 2nd, 3rd, 4th Sts; St. Matthew's R.C. Church. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers six residential blocks in the western part of the borough of National Park, on the street grid that runs north-west to south-east, square to the Delaware River front. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. Columbia Boulevard runs down the middle of the sheet, crossed by Wesley Avenue at the top, then Asbury Avenue, Simpson Avenue, Hessian Avenue and Lakehurst Avenue at the bottom; 4th Street runs along the left edge with only its eastern side drawn, and a short length of Monument Avenue cuts across the top left corner, where the edge of sheet 4 is outlined. The blocks are numbered 139, 144, 151, 152, 159, 160, 166 and 179A and are divided into long, narrow building lots numbered in the 600s. Most lots are empty; the buildings drawn are scattered frame dwellings of one to two and a half storeys with small auto garages and sheds, a few concrete-block outbuildings, and one institution, the 1st M.E. Church on Asbury Avenue west of Columbia Boulevard, heated by furnace and lit by electricity. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are shown along the streets, with fire hydrants at several corners. The sheet's scale bar is printed in Hessian Avenue east of Columbia Boulevard. Adjoining sheets are 4 at the top, 5 on the right, 10 lower right and 12 lower left.
notes: Columbia Boulevard on this sheet is the street now called North 5th Street and South 5th Street; today's Columbia Boulevard is a different street to the north (Columbia Avenue and East Columbia Boulevard on sheets 3 to 6).
1st M.E. Church on Asbury Avenue west of Columbia Boulevard.

50 ft. Pilot sheet. Wesley, Asbury, Simpson, Hessian, Lakehurst Avs crossed by Columbia Blvd (today North/South 5th Street) and 4th St at the left edge. Scale bar printed in Hessian Av. One part. Hessian Av left out of control after review (0.69 -> 0.38 m RMSE without it).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers a block-and-a-half wide strip of central National Park, from Simpson Avenue at the top to Princeton Avenue and the lower edge, on the grid that runs north-west to south-east. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Grove Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and is crossed by Simpson Avenue, Cookman Avenue, Pitman Avenue, Hessian Avenue, Lakehurst Avenue and Princeton Avenue; Hessian Avenue is drawn about 100 feet wide with 8 inch water pipe. Saint Johns Walk runs down the right side between Cookman and Hessian Avenues and Temple Place along the right edge below. The blocks are numbered 152, 160, 161, 167, 175, 176, 179A, 179B, 182 and 183. The upper left holds a fire department building with cement floor, a store and several dwellings; the middle of the right half is built with small frame dwellings and garages on narrow lots; much of the lower half is open land divided into lots. The principal institution is the National Park Public School, lighted by electricity and heated by steam, with a Public School Annex and a second annex building on Grove Avenue between Lakehurst and Princeton Avenues. At the right edge a Camp Meeting Ground with a pavilion is lettered on block 146. A standpipe of 100,000 gallon capacity stands in block 179A. The scale bar is at the foot of the sheet, and the adjoining sheets are 9 at the upper left, 5 at the top, 11 at the right and 12 below.
notes: Grove Avenue is Grove Avenue north of Hessian Avenue and South Grove Avenue south of it in OpenStreetMap; St. Johns Walk, written out in the street names, is Saint Johns Walk in OpenStreetMap.
Hessian Avenue junctions were left out of the control: they fell about 4 m from the drawn centre, while the other points fit to 0.24 m.

50 ft. Simpson, Cookman, Pitman, Hessian, Lakehurst, Princeton Avs; Grove Av; St. Johns Walk; Temple Pl; National Park Public School. One part; Hessian Av left out of control (modern junctions about 4 m off the drawn centre).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the south-eastern part of the main grid of National Park, from Asbury Avenue at the top to Princeton Avenue at the bottom, on the street grid that runs north-west to south-east. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, as the compass rose at the left edge shows. Asbury, Cookman, Pitman, Hessian, Lakehurst and Princeton Avenues cross the sheet; St. James Walk and Oak Avenue run down the upper half, Luther Avenue down the lower half, with Temple Place along the left edge and Lincoln Avenue on a slanting line at the right edge, where it meets the 50 foot margin of sheet 14. Hessian Avenue is about 100 feet wide and carries a 6 inch and an 8 inch water pipe. The blocks are numbered 155, 156, 163, 164, 169, 170, 177, 178, 179C, 179D, 184 and 185, divided into narrow lots numbered in the 800s. The upper blocks between Asbury and Hessian Avenues hold small frame dwellings and garages, with one dwelling coloured as a concrete-block building; the lower blocks south of Hessian Avenue are mostly empty lots, with a row of dwellings along Hessian Avenue east of Luther Avenue. The oval stamp of National Park, N.J. sits in block 156. The left margin lettered 146 and Camp Meeting Ground belongs to sheet 10, and the scale bar is printed in Princeton Avenue. Adjoining sheets are 5 and 6 at the top, 13 on the right, 14 on the lower right and 10 on the left.
notes: Lincoln Avenue is South Lincoln Avenue and North Lincoln Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Saint James Walk is the same in OpenStreetMap.
Hessian Avenue junctions were not used for control: the modern Hessian Avenue line sits about 4 m from the drawn centre on the neighbouring sheet 10.
50 ft. Asbury, Cookman, Pitman, Hessian, Lakehurst, Princeton Avs; St. James Walk, Oak, Luther, Lincoln Avs; Temple Pl. One part; Hessian Av left out of control.

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 12 is the upper right of the sheet, inside a heavy dividing line: the south-western blocks of National Park's street grid, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Hessian Avenue, drawn about 100 feet wide, crosses the top of the part, with Lakehurst Avenue and Princeton Avenue below it; 2nd Street runs down the left side along the dividing line, 3rd Street ends at Hessian Avenue, and 4th Street crosses all three avenues towards the right edge. Woodlawn Avenue leaves Princeton Avenue southward in the middle and reappears as a curving street at the lower right. The blocks are numbered 157, 158, 165, 166, 173 and 174, with large lots 180 and 181 to the south; they are laid out in narrow lots, most of them empty, with scattered dwellings and auto garages. A printing shop stands on Hessian Avenue between 3rd and 4th Streets, and a house named Sylvia on Lakehurst Avenue. Water pipes are shown along each avenue. Sheets 8 and 9 adjoin at the top and right; the rest of sheet 12, beyond the dividing line, shows the river bank and Woodbury Creek at another angle.
notes: 4th Street is drawn with a jog at Lakehurst Avenue that today's street does not have; that junction was left out of the fit.
Hessian Avenue is drawn 100 feet wide.

100 ft. Three parts divided by heavy lines: part 1 (main, north-up compass) Woodbury Creek, Peacock Tract on Riverview Av, Prospect, Liberty, Grove Av, Delaware Dredging Co.; part 2 (upper right) 2nd to 4th Sts, Hessian, Lakehurst, Princeton, Woodlawn Avs; part 3 (left strip) river-bank summer cottages south of the end of Hessian Av. Only part 2 placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: main part: Woodbury Creek, Peacock Tract on Riverview Av, Prospect, Liberty and Grove Avs, Delaware Dredging Co. (modern Riverview Avenue, Prospect Street, Liberty Street and South Grove Avenue junctions disagree with the drawing by 10 to 25 m (a trial fit gave 3.5 px/ft against 3.95); needs hand-picked parcel corners of the Peacock Tract lots and a check of which modern streets keep the 1926 lines).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: left strip: river-bank summer cottages south of the west end of Hessian Av (no street junction; only the end of Hessian Av is drawn; needs step 6b: hand-picked points at the Hessian Av end and parcel corners, if any survive).

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the eastern part of the borough of National Park, from the main grid in the upper left to the diagonal streets that fan out south-east of Red Bank Avenue. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 90 degrees from sheets 3 to 11, so that the streets lettered Simpson, Asbury, Wesley, East Columbia and Philadelphia run up and down the page and are crossed by Lincoln, Girard and Jefferson Avenues; the compass rose at lower left shows north to the upper right. Red Bank or Belmont Avenue crosses the sheet on a diagonal from lower left to upper right and carries the dash-dot line of the borough boundary, which turns up the right side of the sheet near Maple Avenue and 10th Street. Southeast of Red Bank Avenue the blocks are long, narrow strips running down to Hazel, Simpson, Asbury, Cedar, East Columbia, Philadelphia, Lincoln and Maple Avenues and Walnut. The numbered blocks run from 197 to 232. Houses are thickly set in blocks 199 to 202 and 208 to 210 along the main grid and thin out to scattered frame dwellings elsewhere; much of the south-eastern area is laid out in lots with few buildings. A fire department building stands on Wesley Avenue at Red Bank Avenue, and the Red Bank Public School, heated by steam and lit by oil lamps, stands in an open tract at lower left. Hessian Avenue, 100 feet wide, forms the left edge of the main grid. Sheet 11 adjoins on the left, sheet 6 at the top and sheet 14 at the lower left.
notes: The sheet is one part; no inset was found. The upper left grid and the south-eastern diagonal blocks fit one transformation (21 points, 1.5 m RMSE).

Red Bank or Belmont Avenue is Red Bank Avenue in OpenStreetMap; East Columbia Boulevard is Columbia Boulevard on the upper grid and Columbia Avenue on the diagonal in OpenStreetMap; Girard, Jefferson and Lincoln Avenues are North Girard, North Jefferson and North Lincoln Avenues.
Philadelphia Avenue jogs where it meets Red Bank Avenue, and OpenStreetMap carries two nodes about 27 m apart there; both fall on the drawn street.
Hessian Avenue was left out of the control because its modern line is about 4 m from the drawn centre (see sheet 10).
100 ft, turned (rotation about +67). Lincoln, Girard, Jefferson Avs, Red Bank or Belmont Av, Hazel, Cedar, E. Columbia Blvd, Philadelphia, Pine, Maple, Walnut. One part, no inset.

sheet-14-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 14 is the main map of the sheet: the south-eastern edge of National Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Red Bank or Belmont Avenue crosses the lower half diagonally to Hessian Avenue, which runs down the right side of the sheet. South-west of the National Park blocks lies a newer tract of large blocks: Watson Avenue and Edwin Avenue parallel to Red Bank Avenue, crossed by Miller Avenue, Atkins Avenue and Elwood Avenue. These blocks, numbered 15 to 24, are divided into deep lots with only scattered dwellings, auto garages and sheds. In the upper right, Princeton Avenue runs from Girard Avenue at the top to Jefferson Avenue, with blocks 12 and 13; Jefferson Avenue continues east of Hessian Avenue. Near the Hessian and Red Bank junction stand a filling station and the Bethany Union Sunday School, and a few dwellings line Hessian Avenue; blocks 16, 17 and 25 are large lots still mostly open. The upper left of the sheet is an inset, part 2. Sheets 11, 12 and 13 adjoin at the top and right.
notes: Printed as 'Red Bank or Belmont Av.'; today Red Bank Avenue.
Watson Avenue is today Watson Street; Elwood Avenue is today's Ellwood Avenue, and today's Ellwood Avenue also takes over part of the line of Edwin Avenue.
Bethany Union Sunday School and a filling station near Hessian Avenue and Red Bank Avenue.

100 ft. Part 1 main map: Red Bank or Belmont Av, Hessian Av, Watson, Miller, Atkins, Elwood, Edwin Avs, Princeton and Jefferson Avs; part 2 inset (upper left): Lincoln, Lake, Girard Avs between Princeton and Hessian Avs. Rotation about +68.

sheet-14-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 14 is an inset in the upper left corner, enclosed by a heavy line, showing four blocks of National Park between Princeton Avenue and Hessian Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch at the same angle as the main map, with north to the upper right. Lincoln Avenue runs along the top, Lake Avenue through the middle and Girard Avenue along the bottom; Princeton Avenue crosses them on the left and Hessian Avenue on the right, and Lakehurst Avenue ends at Lincoln Avenue at the top. The blocks are numbered 171, 186, 187 and 188, divided into narrow lots with a few dwellings and auto garages, most of them empty; a garage and one store stand near Hessian Avenue. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches run along the avenues, with hydrants at the corners. The inset joins sheet 11 at the top and sheet 13 to the right.
notes: Lincoln Avenue and Girard Avenue are today South Lincoln Avenue and South Girard Avenue.

100 ft. Part 1 main map: Red Bank or Belmont Av, Hessian Av, Watson, Miller, Atkins, Elwood, Edwin Avs, Princeton and Jefferson Avs; part 2 inset (upper left): Lincoln, Lake, Girard Avs between Princeton and Hessian Avs. Rotation about +68.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the village of Verga in West Deptford Township, south-east of National Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. Crown Point Road runs down the sheet from top to bottom; east of it a small grid of blocks lies between Wilson Avenue at the top, Hanold Avenue and Male Avenue, with Verga Avenue running parallel to Crown Point Road. West of the road, Light House Road, Brewer Avenue and Hessian Avenue run diagonally down to the lower left, crossed there by Warren Avenue, Burkett Avenue, Pedan Avenue and Speigle Avenue. The blocks are numbered 25 to 39; those along Crown Point Road and in the eastern grid hold dwellings, auto garages and coops, and the western blocks along Brewer and Hessian Avenues hold scattered dwellings on deep lots, with large lots 32, 33 and 34 still open. Institutions are the Welfare M.E. Church at Crown Point Road and Male Avenue, the fire department of the Verga Fire Co. and town hall on Crown Point Road, and a school at the top right corner. A hall stands on Speigle Avenue. Water pipes are not shown in the village, which had no water facilities in 1926.
notes: Hanold Avenue is today Hannold Avenue, Male Avenue is Mail Avenue, Pedan Avenue is Peden Avenue and Speigle Avenue is Spiegle Avenue.
Light House Road and Wilson Avenue are not in today's street network.
Hessian Avenue and Peden Avenue meet today about 70 feet east of where the sheet draws Pedan Avenue reaching Hessian Avenue; that junction was left out of the fit.
